entries.text: Chicago have shipped thirty-six goals in nine games, four a night, and Montreal are barely tidier at 3.78 against. The Canadiens have scored twenty- eight in nine and the Blackhawks twenty-one, and both goal differentials are deep in the red. In a game projecting past six and a half total goals, both teams reaching two is the cleanest way in.
entries.availability: Neither the NHL schedule nor the team summary report carries a roster or injury list for this fixture, so no absentee is named.

entries.text: Tampa Bay have been the sharpest team in the Eastern Conference so far: 7-2-0 for fourteen points in nine games, thirty-one goals scored against twenty-three allowed. Colorado have eleven points from ten and have already dropped five of them. The Lightning travel to Ball Arena as the better side on every number on the official sheet, so take them outright.
entries.availability: Colorado's goals for and against were not returned in the portion of the official team summary read, which is flagged on this fixture; no injury data is published on that endpoint either.

entries.text: Philadelphia have managed twenty goals in twelve outings, the thinnest scoring rate anywhere in the official team summary at 1.67 per game, and they arrive at 3-6-3 having already conceded thirty-six. Anaheim are 4-6-0 and score 2.70 a night. Two sides this blunt should not combine for seven, so take under 6.5 goals at the Xfinity Mobile Arena.
entries.availability: The NHL schedule and team-summary endpoints read for this desk publish no injury or scratch list, so no absence is claimed for either side.

entries.event: Los Angeles Kings @ New Jersey Devils
entries.text: New Jersey are 6-4-0 and comfortably the better team here, but the shape of this one is a grind rather than a shootout. Los Angeles have scored twenty goals in eight games, a feeble 2.50 per night, and have won twice all season. Six and a quarter goals is the honest expectation, which makes under 7.5 at the Prudential Center the pick.
entries.availability: No official injury report accompanies either the schedule feed or the team summary report, so neither lineup is adjusted.

entries.text: Boston own the best record in the whole official summary at 8-2-1 for seventeen points, and the underlying split is just as strong: forty-two goals scored, twenty-two conceded, a plus-twenty swing in eleven games. San Jose are 6-4-1 but are minus-four on the same measure, thirty-two for and thirty-six against. Back the Bruins on the money line at TD Garden.
entries.availability: The team summary report carries no injury column, so no Bruins or Sharks absence is factored into this price.

entries.text: This is the one tight defensive matchup on the slate. The Rangers are 7-4-1 and have allowed just twenty-nine goals in twelve games, 2.42 a night, the best rate among tonight's travelling sides. Ottawa sit 7-4-0 with an almost level differential, twenty-nine for and thirty against. Expect a close, low-event night in Canada: under 6.5 goals.
entries.availability: No official availability list was published alongside either team's summary line, so the price assumes both squads as rostered.

entries.event: Tampa Bay Rays @ Milwaukee Brewers — World Series Game 1
entries.text: Milwaukee were the best regular-season team in baseball at 103-59 and they open the Series at home, where they went 55-26. Tampa Bay are no soft touch though: 98-64 with a 43-38 road record and only eighty-six runs of separation across the whole year. Opening nights are rarely blowouts, so take the Rays with a run and a half of insurance.
entries.availability: The schedule endpoint returned no probable starting pitcher and no injury list for Game 1, so neither rotation nor bullpen availability is priced in.

entries.event: Tampa Bay Rays @ Milwaukee Brewers — World Series Game 2
entries.text: Game 2 is the one Tampa Bay genuinely have to avoid losing badly, and the run line is where their season profile pays. The Rays scored 736 and allowed 650 across 162 games, a tidy 90-72 Pythagorean line that sits far closer to Milwaukee than the raw records suggest. A second straight night at American Family Field still looks like a one-run game: Rays plus 1.5.
entries.availability: No probable starters were listed for Game 2 on the official schedule feed, and no injury report is attached to it.

entries.event: Milwaukee Brewers @ Tampa Bay Rays — World Series Game 3
entries.text: The Series moves to Tropicana Field and the price flips almost to a coin. Milwaukee were 48-33 away from home and finished 8-2 over their last ten, with 832 runs scored against 618 allowed; Tampa Bay were 55-26 at home but split their last ten 5-5. The Brewers are the fractionally better team even on the road, so take them on the money line.
entries.availability: Neither probable pitchers nor an injury list were published on the schedule endpoint for Game 3, so this stays a Medium-confidence call.

entries.event: Zalgiris Kaunas v LDLC ASVEL Villeurbanne
entries.text: Both clubs are 2-4 after six rounds, but the splits are not alike. Zalgiris have conceded 517 points against 490 scored, minus 4.5 a game; ASVEL are minus 7.5, with 572 conceded and the worst defence in the bottom half of the table. Add Zalgirio Arena, one of the loudest rooms in Europe, and the home side are the play.
entries.availability: The EuroLeague schedule and standings feeds carry no roster, rotation or injury field, so no absence is claimed for either club.

entries.event: Olympiacos Piraeus v Fenerbahce Tarfin Istanbul
entries.text: This is the round's genuine heavyweight tie and the numbers refuse to separate them. Olympiacos and Fenerbahce are both 5-1; the Greeks have scored more, 564 to 501, while the Turkish side have defended better, conceding only 447. Home court at SUNEL Arena is the entire edge, so Olympiacos get the narrowest of nods in a near coin-flip.
entries.availability: Neither club's availability is published on the official EuroLeague feeds, so this stays Medium rather than being pushed higher.

entries.text: Valencia are 4-2 and the best attacking team in the round with 583 points from six games, plus 7.7 a night. Paris are 1-5 and minus 6.8, conceding 545. Even allowing the Adidas Arena crowd its two and a half points, the gap projects at twelve, which makes the Spanish side giving 11.5 the better value than a money line too short to quote.
entries.availability: No injury or availability list is published on the EuroLeague feeds read, so this is priced on season point differential alone and held at Medium.

entries.event: Arthur Fils v Alex Michelsen — Quarter-final
entries.text: Arthur Fils is the standout name left in Brussels, ranked tenth with 3,325 ranking points against Alex Michelsen's 1,370 from thirty-seventh. That is a near two-and-a-half-fold advantage on the official ladder and the clearest ranking gap of any quarter-final on either tour today. The Frenchman to win the match is the straightforward selection.
entries.availability: No retirement, walkover or medical timeout is noted against either player on the official Brussels order of play.

entries.event: Flavio Cobolli v Brandon Nakashima — Quarter-final
entries.market: Set Handicap Flavio Cobolli -1.5 / Brandon Nakashima +1.5
entries.text: Flavio Cobolli is the rightful favourite in Lyon with 3,640 ranking points to Brandon Nakashima's 2,375, but that gap is far too narrow to expect a tidy straight-sets afternoon. The American sits seventeenth in the world and these are two baseliners inside a thousand points of each other. Take Nakashima with a set and a half of start.
entries.availability: The ATP daily schedule and the singles rankings page carry no withdrawal or medical note for either player.

entries.event: Luca Van Assche v Lorenzo Musetti — Quarter-final
entries.text: Lorenzo Musetti holds 1,870 ranking points from twenty-sixth in the world against Luca Van Assche's 1,065 from forty-eighth, a real but not overwhelming edge on the Lyon hard court. The Italian has the better season behind him and the higher ceiling in a long rally, so he is the selection — without the confidence that a bigger ranking gap would buy.
entries.availability: The Lyon daily schedule lists no injury, withdrawal or late change for either player.

entries.event: David Gilbert v Mark Williams — Match 59 · Quarter-final (best of 11)
entries.text: Mark Williams arrives with an 8-2 frame record in Belfast against David Gilbert's 8-5, and the Welshman is comfortably the more ruthless closer of the two. A race to six that ends 6-2 or 6-3 keeps the match inside nine and a half frames, which is where the value sits rather than on a money line too short to quote.
entries.availability: No fitness or withdrawal note appears against either player on the official tournament draw.

entries.event: Jak Jones v Scott Donaldson — Match 60 · Quarter-final (best of 11)
entries.text: Scott Donaldson has been the cleaner scorer in Belfast, taking eight frames and dropping only three across the second and third rounds. Jak Jones comes in off a 4-2 third-round win but his earlier frame line is not on the published draw, so the weight of visible evidence sits firmly with the Scot. Donaldson to win the quarter-final.
entries.availability: World Snooker Tour publishes no withdrawal or fitness note for either player on this draw page. The uneven frame window is flagged on the fixture.

entries.event: Kyren Wilson v Sam Craigie — Match 61 · Semi-final (best of 11)
entries.text: Kyren Wilson and Sam Craigie arrive at the semi-final with identical 10-4 frame records across the third round and quarter-finals, which is why the match price is effectively a coin toss. When two players are scoring this evenly a long decider is less likely than it looks, so the total staying under 9.5 frames is the more sensible way in.
entries.availability: World Snooker Tour lists no injury or availability note for either player.

entries.competition: FIA Formula One World Championship 2026 — Round 21
entries.event: FORMULA 1 MSC CRUISES UNITED STATES GRAND PRIX 2026
entries.text: Max Verstappen has won two of the last five grands prix, Singapore and Bahrain, more than anyone else on the grid, yet he sits only fourth in the championship on 221 points behind Kimi Antonelli's 340. That combination — elite recent race-winning form on a circuit he has owned, without the championship points to shorten him — makes a Verstappen podium at Austin the selection.
entries.availability: Qualifying does not run until 21:00 UTC on 24 October, so no grid position exists yet, and no driver change is listed on the official event page.
